comdynamite

Methods that link traits, phylogenies, biogeography and metacommunities in R, to analyse data and to simulate it.

The simulations work at the level of populations in ecological time: abundances in every site grow, compete and disperse, and, when asked, each population carries the genetic means of one or more traits that evolve by selection and drift under quantitative genetics (Lande 1979), with a covariance matrix G per species. Lineages can split into new species inside the metacommunity, so the same run gives communities, trait distributions of individuals and the true phylogeny. Because the truth is known, the analysis functions of the package can be tested on these simulations before they are applied to field data.

What do you want to do?

Analyse data

Question Functions Article
Which clades respond to the environment or to biogeographic events? node_contrasts(), biogeography_matrix(), node_test() Analysing clades
Does phylogenetic composition follow the environment across the whole tree? pcc_test(), pcps_test(), phylo_beta_test() Testing the whole tree
Which phylogenetic axis relates to a predictor? phylo_vector() Analysing clades
How much of trait or phylogenetic variation is due to environment and space? trait_partition(), plot_trait_partition() Analysing clades
My sites are neighbours: which null model? torus_permutations(), rigid_permutations(), patch_permutations() Analysing clades
How do I format my own data? Preparing your data

Simulate data

Question Functions Article
Dynamics with growth, competition and dispersal, as in Thompson et al. (2020) simulate_metacommunity() Get started
Static communities along gradients simulate_static(), simulate_logistic() Testing the whole tree
Assembly by rules, without dynamics, as in Kraft et al. (2007) assemble_community() Watching assembly
Traits with phylogenetic signal or under Ornstein-Uhlenbeck regimes species_traits(), trait_ou() Get started
Local adaptation, migration load and evolutionary rescue, with one or several traits evolution_control(), genetic_matrices(), maladaptation() Quantitative genetics in the metacommunity
Speciation inside the metacommunity, with the full and reconstructed trees simulate_evolving_metacommunity(), speciation_control()
Individuals sampled from simulated populations, and tests of drift sample_individuals(), drift_test()
Does a method work? Type I error and power by simulation all of the above Evaluating methods

In R, ?comdynamite gives the same map.

Installation 

install.packages("comdynamite", repos = c("https://diogoprov.r-universe.dev",
                                          "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
# or
remotes::install_github("diogoprov/comdynamite")

Large analyses

The permutations of pcc_test(), pcps_test(), phylo_beta_test() and trait_partition() run in parallel when you choose a plan with the future package, and results can be reproduced with set.seed() for any number of workers. node_test() has its own cores argument: it took about 4 minutes with 600 species, 100 sites and 999 permutations on one core.

future::plan(future::multisession, workers = 4)

Inputs can be tibbles of numeric columns, and as.data.frame() or tibble::as_tibble() turn results into tables.

Example 

library(comdynamite)
set.seed(1)
tr <- treeshapesim::sim_tree_shape(40)
sim <- simulate_metacommunity(
  landscape  = landscape_implicit(50),
  traits     = species_traits(tr, lambda = 1),
  alpha      = competition_matrix(tr, type = "phylo"),
  dispersal  = 0.01,
  n_steps    = 1000
)
sim$abundance  # sites x species

The website has the articles and the function reference. To read the vignettes in R, install with build_vignettes = TRUE.

Related packages

  • mcomsimr, by Patrick Thompson, is the original R implementation of the model of Thompson et al. (2020). comdynamite was written independently from the published equations. It differs in its conventions (sigma is the standard deviation of the Gaussian response, so it equals sqrt(2) times the niche breadth of Thompson et al.; alpha[j, k] is the effect of species k on species j) and adds phylogenetic traits and competition, grid landscapes on a torus with their restricted permutations, and abundances recorded over time.

  • gen3sis (Hagen et al.

    1. is a general engine for eco-evolutionary simulations on landscapes that change over geological time. Speciation, extinction, dispersal and trait evolution are simulated, so the phylogeny is an outcome of the simulation, and the ecological rules are functions that the user writes. In comdynamite the phylogeny is an input: the tree is fixed, traits are placed on it with a chosen phylogenetic signal, and a fixed population model runs over ecological time (no speciation). This is what simulation studies of methods need, because tree shape and phylogenetic signal can be set independently and replicates can be paired by tree across scenarios. The two can be combined: a phylogeny produced by gen3sis can be used as the regional pool of a comdynamite simulation.

  • treeshapesim simulates trees with separately controlled imbalance and branching times, to use as regional pools in comdynamite. Tree shape can then be a factor in the design of a simulation study:

    tr <- treeshapesim::sim_tree_shape(40, beta = -1, c = -0.5)
sim <- simulate_metacommunity(landscape_implicit(20), species_traits(tr, lambda = 1),
                              competition_matrix(tr, type = "phylo"),
                              dispersal = 0.01, n_steps = 1000)

Citation

Provete, D. B. (2026). comdynamite: Linking traits, phylogenies and biogeography in metacommunities. R package. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23993533

This DOI always points to the latest version; each release also has its own DOI on Zenodo. In R, citation("comdynamite") gives the entry with the installed version.
